title: Extension from a normal dense open into a finite target
statement: Let $S,X,E$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $n:X\to S$ be a morphism, and let $p:E\to S$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Assume $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and every local ring of $X$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion with dense image [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every morphism $a:U\to E$ with $p\circ a=n\circ j$, there is a unique morphism $b:X\to E$ such that $p\circ b=n$ and $b\circ j=a$. Equivalently, restriction induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,E)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(U,E)$. No normality, reducedness or nonemptiness of $E$, no finiteness of $n$, and no separatedness of $S$ is assumed; the empty scheme $X$ is allowed.

source.place: Tags 035I (morphisms-lemma-characterize-normalization: relative-normalization extension) and 01RH (morphisms-lemma-equality-of-morphisms: relative separated uniqueness), applied to a dense open of a locally Noetherian normal source.

proof.text: Identify $U$ with its open image using [def-weil-open-immersion]. The morphism $j$ is quasi-compact: for any affine open $A\subset X$, the remark in [pqf-def-locnoeth] makes $A$ locally Noetherian, and affineness makes it quasi-compact, so it is a Noetherian scheme. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], its open subscheme $U\cap A$ is quasi-compact. This is exactly the affine test in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

For quasi-separatedness, $j$ is a monomorphism: a morphism factoring through an open subscheme has a unique such factorization, on both its space and restricted structure sheaf. Thus $U\times_XU\cong U$ with both projections the identity, by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Its diagonal is an isomorphism and hence quasi-compact, proving quasi-separatedness by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. This checks the hypotheses for relative normalization without assuming that $X$ itself is quasi-compact.

source.place: Definition of open immersion and elementary diagonal computation; the universal property of fibre products, Tag 01JP

proof.text: Form $T=E\times_S X$ with projections $r:T\to E$ and $q:T\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The finite morphism $p$ is integral by [pqf-lem-finite-integral-lft], and its base change $q$ is integral by [lem-sbc-integral-morphism-base-change]. In particular $q$ is affine, by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. The equality $p\circ a=n\circ j$ supplies the unique lift $\alpha=(a,j):U\to T$, with $r\circ\alpha=a$ and $q\circ\alpha=j$. No property of $n$ beyond being a morphism is used.

source.place: Tags 01WJ (lemma-finite-integral), 01WL (lemma-base-change-finite); fibre-product universal property, Schemes Tag 01JP

proof.text:
Take the relative normalization $U\xrightarrow{i}N\xrightarrow{
u}X$ of $j$, so $
u\circ i=j$ [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization]. The local rings of $X$ are integrally closed domains and $U$ is dense, so [lem-sbc-normalization-dense-open] says that $
u$ is an isomorphism, including when $X$ is empty or disconnected. Apply [lem-sbc-relative-normalization-universal-property] to the factorization $j=q\circ\alpha$ through the integral morphism $q$. It gives $d:N	o T$ satisfying $d\circ i=\alpha$ and $q\circ d=
u$. These inputs identify the actual normalization of $j$, not a normalization of $E$ or of $n$.

source.place: Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization); the existing dense-open normalization identification, Tags 0357 and 0AB1

proof.text:
Put $s=d\circ
u^{-1}:X	o T$ and $b=r\circ s$. Then $q\circ s=
u\circ
u^{-1}=1_X$, and $
u^{-1}\circ j=i$, so $s\circ j=d\circ i=\alpha$. Using the pullback equation $p\circ r=n\circ q$ gives $p\circ b=n\circ q\circ s=n$, and $b\circ j=r\circ\alpha=a$. All equalities follow by composition of the two equations from the preceding step and the inverse identities; this constructs the required extension.

proof.text:
For uniqueness, let $b_1,b_2:X	o E$ satisfy $p\circ b_k=n$ and $b_k\circ j=a$. Their pullback lifts $s_k=(b_k,1_X):X	o T$ exist and obey $q\circ s_k=1_X$ and $s_k\circ j=\alpha$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Set $d_k=s_k\circ
u:N	o T$. Then $q\circ d_k=
u$ and $d_k\circ i=s_k\circ j=\alpha$. Since $q$ is affine, the uniqueness clause of [lem-sbc-relative-normalization-universal-property] gives $d_1=d_2$. Composing with $
u^{-1}$ and then $r$ gives $b_1=b_2$. Existence and uniqueness say exactly that restriction on the stated $S$-Hom sets is bijective. The construction also applies to $X=\varnothing$: normalization, pullbacks and these equations require no chosen point. If $E=\varnothing$ and $X
e\varnothing$, density makes $U
e\varnothing$, so no initial morphism $a$ exists and the assertion is vacuous.
